summary.title: Face recognition with OpenCV, Python, and deep learning
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a face recognition pipeline in Python using dlib's 128-d deep metric embeddings via the face_recognition library, with OpenCV for images and video.
keywords: labeled faces in the wild accuracy
how to recognize faces in images
takeaways: Deep metric learning maps each face to a 128-d feature vector so that same-person faces lie close together.
Build a known-face database by encoding a labeled image dataset into encodings.pickle with face_recognition and dlib.
Recognize faces by comparing a new face encoding to known encodings and taking a vote among matches.
Choose hog for speed on CPU or Raspberry Pi and cnn for accuracy when a GPU is available.
summary.summary: This PyImageSearch tutorial explains how deep learning face recognition works using dlib's pretrained network, which outputs 128-d embeddings trained with triplets. It walks through installing dlib, face_recognition and imutils, then building a dataset of six Jurassic Park characters and encoding each face with encode_faces.py. The recognition section shows how compare_faces and a simple vote count assign names to faces in images, with video recognition scripts covered in the project structure. The page is a long, hands-on code walkthrough with command-line examples and timing notes for CPU and GPU.
